 Kings vs. Lakers: Something wicked this way comes
 The Kings could set a record for futility in tonight's game, and that's saying something when it comes to the Kings. 
 By Akis Yerocostas | 19 Comments | Nov 20, 2026 
 Nov 4, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers forward/guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts to a call during the fourth quarter of the game against the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-Imagn Images
 After an 0-7 homestand, the Kings now get to visit the 13-3 Los Angeles Lakers on the road, where their 29th ranked defense will somehow hope to contain a supercharged Luka Doncic who is currently averaging 38.1 points a game.
 Fun.
 Who: Sacramento Kings (1-13) vs. L.A. Lakers (13-3).
 Where: Crypto.com Arena, Los Angeles, CA
 When: 7 PM PDT / 10 PM EDT
 Watch: NBCSCA / League Pass
 The 1990-91 Sacramento Kings set the standard for the worst start in franchise history at 1-13.  In a team with as large of a history of failure, the fact that this year’s team has not only tied it but has a chance to break that record by a significant amount is simply remarkable but here we are.  That 1990-91 team went on to win 25 games, but it should be noted that they won 24 of those games at home.  This year’s Kings team hasn’t managed to win a single one at home, so maybe it’s a good thing that tonight’s game is on the road.
 Then again, their opponent is a revamped Lakers squad that is currently tied for the best record in the league. It turns out that Luka Doncic was out of shape, and getting in shape has locked an even higher level of play.  Through 16 games, he’s averaging 38.1 points on 46.6% from the field and 38.3% from three, as well as 7.6 assists, 7 rebounds and 1.9 steals a game.  The Lakers are playing their highest level of basketball in years and are also probably a little angry after dropping a rare bad loss to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday.  The Kings have faced the Lakers once already this season and gave the Kings a 116-103 loss to start off their homestand.
 If it seems like I’m feeling particularly down about this Kings team, it’s because it’s really hard for me to see a light at the end of this tunnel right now.  This team isn’t playing with energy or passion, and the schedule is hardly letting up either.  I mentioned this the other day, but it’s not even just that the Kings aren’t winning, they’re barely ever even in the lead.  In fact, I went back and looked at the Kings recent homestand; In 336 minutes of game action, the Kings only led for 31 minutes and 15 seconds.  That’s just 9.3% of the time.
 The new lottery rules make it so that even if this team ends up with a historically bad record (they have a legitimate chance of being 1-19 a quarter of the way through the season), they could still fall all the way to the 12th pick in the draft.  Our vets are simply waiting to get traded to move on to greener pastures, but they’re also playing so poorly that nobody will want to take them, which only exacerbates the issue.  Everyone in and around the Kings seems to know that it’s only a matter of when and not if Doug Christie gets fired as coach, but for now he’s still here as well.  To make matters worse, the only changes our GM is making seem to be nonsensical, like adding a 36 year old fourth string Center when the team has been desperate for a backup PG since Ben Simmons tore his Achilles in preseason.
 Right now Darius Acuff Jr. is pretty much the only reason to be watching Kings basketball.  He’s hardly a perfect player;  His defense is as bad as advertised and he can get sloppy with some of his decision making on the other end, but he’s also the only player that generates any sort of excitement or buzz about this team going forward.  His shotmaking and playmaking ability for a rookie is off the charts, and he will no doubt set records during his time here.  But it will all be meaningless if the Kings can’t build a winning team around him.  I worry that the lack of structure and the sheer incompetence that currently surrounds him will be too much to overcome.
 Anyway, beat LA, I guess.
 Prediction: Lakers 125, Kings 99

 I’ve been a die hard fan since 85′. The Reggie Theus, Mark Olberding, LaSalle Thompson era. I survived the 2008-2009 Kings. This season seems like the worst by far. At least in 2008-2009 there were several young guys and you knew they were going to get a high draft pick which turned out to be ROY Tyreke Evans, the 20-5-5 phenom. This roster doesn’t provide a lot of hope for the future outside of the rookie and the vets aren’t likely to fetch much value. The organization won’t be able to attract talent even as their cap sheet frees up. To cap it off, their terrible record actually hurts their draft value. This season is killing even this most die hard of fans.
As far as Acuff, I try to be optimistic but I’m not sold. Even the worst team has a top scorer. Somebody has to take and make shots and I guess he’s the guy. Efficiency is still questionable and defense is bad. Is he the next version of Trae Young? Maybe. Do you build your franchise around that? No. Maybe I’m burnt by the Tyreke hype in 2009-2010 when he was one of the only rookies to post a 20-5-5 line, with LeBron being the main comp.
I’ll turn on the game tonight and hopelessly root for the Kings to beat the Lakers as after all, tonight the Kings are my favorite and second favorite (whoever is playing the Lakers) team tonight.
